overview: A single-page State Department cross-reference sheet concerning the legal status of the Kwantung Leased Territory. It points to a telegram dated April 4, 1941, reporting information from the U.S. consul at Dairen clarifying that, although Japan exercised jurisdiction and administrative authority in the leased area, the United States did not recognize it as an integral part of the Japanese Empire.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the status of the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.from: U.S. Consul at Dairen (source of referenced information)
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to a telegram clarifying the U.S. position on Japanese authority and sovereignty in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference points to telegram no. 215 of April 4, 1941, filed as 894c.5151/8. The referenced information states that Japan's lease permitted it to exercise jurisdictional and administrative authority in the Kwantung Leased Territory, but that the United States did not regard the territory as an integral part of the Japanese Empire.

interest: The document succinctly records an important distinction in U.S. diplomacy between recognizing Japan's administrative jurisdiction under a lease and recognizing Japanese territorial sovereignty. Its cross-reference to a separately filed telegram also illustrates how the State Department's decimal filing system connected documents classified under different subjects, making the sheet useful for reconstructing the archival trail of U.S. policy toward Japan's position in southern Manchuria.
